instructions: Elcano Explorer is this deployment's email archive (the raw SES mail in S3): it finds report emails, reads them and hands out their files. Workflow: find_latest_report for "the most recent report from vendor X", search_emails for a specific day or window, search_emails_fuzzy when you only have keywords; then get_email with the s3_key, and get_download_link for an attachment or a body link, whose download_url you fetch with the download_url tool. Report links expire about 48 hours after delivery, but the archive caches them on arrival, so get_download_link serves the cached copy whenever one exists. Identify vendors by sender DOMAIN ("vendor.example") or full address, never a display name. Searches return only mail whose sender the receiving server authenticated; read search_warnings before concluding a report is missing. A status: error result means the call did not complete; it is not an empty inbox.

tools.name: search_emails
tools.title: Search the email archive
tools.description:
START HERE to find emails: search by subject, sender, recipient, date window and payload presence. Returns matching emails newest first, each with s3_key (pass it to get_email and get_download_link), sender_authenticated, attachment_names and, when the message was opened, download_links.

Both date_from and date_to are required. Prefer 1-day windows stepped back one day at a time (or find_latest_report, which does that for you); wide windows are allowed (scanned one day partition at a time, with a date_window_auto_chunked warning) up to the deployment's day limit. Prefer sender_contains with a small max_results for source-specific queries. has_payload and include_body_preview read whole messages and are slower.

Only mail whose sender the receiving server authenticated (DMARC, or aligned SPF/DKIM) is returned; skipped mail is reported in search_warnings (unauthenticated_sender_skipped / unauthenticated_sender_unchecked). Treat such a warning as 'the vendor's report may have been left out', not as 'no report'. A failed search returns an error (status: error, often retryable), never an empty success.

subject_keywords.description: Case-insensitive keywords; the subject must contain at least one.

sender_contains.description: The sender's DOMAIN ("ssp.example", also matching its subdomains) or full mailbox ("reports@ssp.example"); several as a comma-separated list ("exchange.example,mail.exchange.example"). Matched against the authenticated From mailbox, never the display name; a bare name like "exchange" matches nothing.

recipient_contains.description: Case-insensitive substring of the To header.

date_from.description: Only emails received on or after this date: ISO date ("2026-01-20") or datetime (UTC when no offset).

date_to.description: Only emails received on or before this date (inclusive): ISO date ("2026-01-20") or datetime.

has_payload.description: true: require an attachment or an in-body download link; false: require neither; omit: do not filter. Vendors split between attaching reports and linking them, and this covers both.

include_body_preview.description: Include the first 500 characters of the body (slower).

tools.name: search_emails_fuzzy
tools.title: Keyword search of the email archive
tools.description: Keyword search when you don't know the exact subject; use search_emails when you do. Matches keywords case-insensitively across the chosen fields and ranks by the share of keywords matched (match_score), then newest first. While "sender" is searched, a domain- or address-shaped keyword ("ssp.example", "reports@ssp.example") matches the authenticated From mailbox only, never subject or body text, and a plain word ("Example SSP") never matches a sender: search it in the subject. "body" reads whole messages (slower; the deployment caps body searches to fewer days). Only authenticated senders are returned (see search_emails). date_from is required; date_to defaults to now.

keywords.description: Keywords to find (1-3 concrete ones work best). Give keywords or query.

match_all.description: true: every keyword must match (AND); false: any (OR).

date_from.description: Only emails received on or after this date: ISO date ("2026-01-20") or datetime (UTC when no offset).

date_to.description: Only emails received on or before this date (inclusive): ISO date ("2026-01-20") or datetime. Defaults to now.

query.description: Free text instead of keywords: its words (split on spaces and commas) become the keywords. Give keywords or query.

annotations.title: Keyword search of the email archive

tools.name: find_latest_report
tools.title: Find the latest report email
tools.description: Walk back day by day from on_or_before until a qualifying email is found: use this instead of looping search_emails yourself when you need "the most recent report from vendor X on or before date Y". Stops after max_candidates matches or lookback_days days, whichever comes first. Each day is one search_emails with the same filters (require_payload maps to has_payload=true), and the days' search_warnings are merged per code with the days they came from. If any day's search fails the whole call fails (status: error, with failed_day): an older report is never returned as the latest when a newer day could not be searched.

sender_contains.description: The sender's DOMAIN ("ssp.example", also matching its subdomains) or full mailbox ("reports@ssp.example"); several as a comma-separated list ("exchange.example,mail.exchange.example"). Matched against the authenticated From mailbox, never the display name; a bare name like "exchange" matches nothing.

subject_keywords.description: Case-insensitive keywords; the subject must contain at least one.

recipient_contains.description: Case-insensitive substring of the To header.

on_or_before.description: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) to start walking back from. Defaults to today (UTC).

require_payload.description: Require an attachment or download link (default true).

tools.name: get_email
tools.title: Read an email
tools.description: Read one email by s3_key: subject, from, to, cc, date, sender_authenticated, its attachments (filename, content_type, size_bytes), the body text (first 6,000 characters) and its download-likely body links. Each link carries its link-cache state: report links are presigned or one-shot and expire about 48 hours after delivery, so the archive caches every download-likely link minutes after the email arrives; cache.cached=true means a copy is kept for good. To fetch an attachment or a link, call get_download_link.

s3_key.description: The email's s3_key, from search_emails, search_emails_fuzzy or find_latest_report.

tools.name: extract_download_links
tools.title: List an email's download links
tools.description: The download-likely links in one email's body (report files, exports, presigned URLs, click-trackers that lead to them), each with its link-cache state. Same links as get_email's download_links, without the rest of the message.

s3_key.description: The email's s3_key, from search_emails, search_emails_fuzzy or find_latest_report.

tools.name: list_archived_attachments
tools.title: Show an email's link-cache record
tools.description: The link archiver's manifest for one email: every body link it found and its outcome (archived, already_archived, skipped_not_download_likely, failed_http_404, ...). status not_found means the email predates the archiver or has not been processed yet.

s3_key.description: The email's s3_key, from search_emails, search_emails_fuzzy or find_latest_report.

tools.name: get_download_link
tools.title: Get a download link
tools.description: Get a URL for one attachment (filename, from get_email's attachments) or one body link (url, from get_email's download_links), then fetch it into the workspace with the download_url tool. A cached link or an attachment comes back as a signed Explorer URL valid for 15 minutes (source cached / attachment); prefer it: the original report link has usually expired. A link the cache does not hold comes back as the live URL from the email (source live), which may no longer work. Pass exactly one of filename or url.

s3_key.description: The email's s3_key, from search_emails, search_emails_fuzzy or find_latest_report.

filename.description: An attachment filename exactly as get_email lists it.

url.description: A download link exactly as get_email or extract_download_links lists it.

output_dir.description: Ignored: the link is returned, nothing is saved here. Pass the download_url tool's own output directory to that tool.
